0.headline: Purple Style Labs IPO to open on Aug 31; 8 investors pick up Rs 306 crore worth shares via anchor book
0.heading: Purple Style Labs IPO to open on Aug 31; 8 investors pick up Rs 306 crore worth shares via anchor book
0.intro: Purple Style Labs IPO | The Abhishek Agarwal-promoted company is looking to raise up to Rs 680 crore through an initial public offering, comprising entirely a fresh issue.
0.body:
Purple Style Labs, the Mumbai-based luxury fashion company operating 14 stores under the Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop brand, has raised Rs 306 crore from eight anchor investors, including Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities and Integrated Core Strategies, on August 28.

The fundraising comes ahead of the IPO opening for public subscription on August 31. The price band has been fixed at Rs 546–575 per share, and the issue will close on September 2.

The Abhishek Agarwal-promoted company is looking to raise up to Rs 680 crore through an initial public offering (IPO), comprising entirely a fresh issue.

Purple Style Labs has allocated 53.21 lakh shares through the anchor book at the upper end of the price band on Friday.

Of the total anchor book, 17.39 lakh shares were allocated to two domestic mutual funds, which applied through three schemes. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerged as the largest buyer among anchor investors, picking up 15.3 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 88 crore.

This was followed by Jupiter Asset Management, which bought over 13 lakh shares worth Rs 75 crore, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, which purchased 11.82 lakh shares worth Rs 68 crore.

Ace investor Madhusudan Kela-backed Singularity AMC acquired an additional 1.73 lakh shares in Purple Style Labs worth nearly Rs 10 crore, while ITI Mutual Fund bought over 2 lakh shares worth Rs 12 crore.

Singularity AMC already held a 1.86 percent stake in the fashion company, while Akash Bhanshali-sponsored Volrado Venture Partners and Mukul Mahavir Agrawal held 2.79 percent and 1.37 percent stakes, respectively. Promoter Abhishek Agarwal owns a 26.09 percent stake in the company.

Purple Style Labs provides curated selections of luxury fashion sourced from 1,109 active designer brands, including Seema Gujral, Anushree Reddy, Amit Aggarwal, and Rohit Gandhi &amp; Rahul Khanna, across women’s wear, men’s wear and other categories, with a focus on wedding and occasion wear.

The company intends to invest Rs 371.1 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds in its subsidiary, PSL Retail, towards expenditure on lease liabilities for Experience Centers and back-end offices in India.

Further, Rs 138.9 crore will be utilised for sales and marketing expenses, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company operates through 14 Experience Centers globally, including 12 in metropolitan cities across India, which are operated on a leave-and-license basis. It also sells through online platforms and participates in events and exhibitions.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are acting as the merchant bankers for the public issue of Purple Style Labs.

1.headline: Jio Platforms, Paras Healthcare, Bharat PET, and 4 other IPOs receive SEBI approval
1.heading: Jio Platforms, Paras Healthcare, Bharat PET, and 4 other IPOs receive SEBI approval
1.intro: Bharat PET, Sadbhav Futuretech, Paramotor Digital Technology, M K Sons Fine Jewels Jio Platforms, Paras Healthcare, and Pushp Brand (India) have approached the SEBI with their IPO documents during March to June period of this year.
1.body:
Seven companies, including Jio Platforms, Paras Healthcare, and Bharat PET among seven companies have received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to go ahead with their IPO plans. The capital markets regulator have also given thumbs up to the IPO proposals of Sadbhav Futuretech, M K Sons Fine Jewels, Paramotor Digital Technology, and Pushp Brand (India).

Bharat PET, Sadbhav Futuretech, Paramotor Digital Technology, M K Sons Fine Jewels, Jio Platforms, Paras Healthcare, and Pushp Brand (India) have approached the SEBI with their IPO documents during March to June period of this year.

The capital markets regulator has issued its observations on the draft document of Paras Healthcare on August 24, Paramotor Digital Technology on August 25, Bharat PET on August 26, and Pushp Brand (India) on August 27, while the observations on the IPO papers of M K Sons Fine Jewels, Sadbhav Futuretech, and Jio Platforms have been issued on August 28, as per the processing status of draft offer documents published for the week ended August 28.

In SEBI parlance, the issuance of observations means the company is allowed to launch its IPO fund raising plan with the next one year in case of regular filing, while the company that files draft documents via confidential route gets 18-month window to float the IPO in the market.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Jio Platforms plans IPO of 27 crore shares
Jio Platforms (JPL), the technology company and a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, is looking to raise funds through an entirely fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component. This means the entire issue proceeds will accrue to the company.

The company has proposed to utilise Rs 27,500 crore of the net IPO proceeds to repay certain debt, with the remaining funds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Reliance Jio Infocomm, a subsidiary of Jio Platforms, served 52.44 crore customers through its telecom network in India as of March 2026. JPL brings together mobile, fixed broadband and digital services on a unified platform, along with data and customer-personalisation capabilities.

Paras Healthcare proposes Rs 1,800-crore IPO
Gurugram-based Paras Healthcare, the hospital chain operating under the Paras Health brand, refiled its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) in June this year, with plans to raise up to Rs 1,800 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).

The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 crore, while the promoter and investors will sell shares worth Rs 1,300 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

Paras Healthcare provides tertiary and quaternary healthcare services through eight hospitals with a total capacity of 2,211 beds across North India, Bihar and Jharkhand. The company has proposed to utilise Rs 375 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards repayment of debt, with the remaining amount earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Bharat PET taps capital markets with Rs 760-crore IPO
Bharat PET, a Delhi-based packaging solutions provider, has moved a step closer to raising up to Rs 760 crore through an initial public offering (IPO) after receiving observations from SEBI.

The public issue will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 120 crore, along with an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 640 crore by the promoters.

The packaging company manufactures PET bottles and jars, preforms, multi-layer co-extruded bottles, caps and closures, and tin containers across its four manufacturing facilities. It has proposed to utilise Rs 50 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards repayment of certain borrowings, Rs 35.8 crore for the purchase of machinery and equipment, and the remaining funds for general corporate purposes.

Sadbhav Futuretech plans IPO with fresh issue and OFS combination
Sadbhav Futuretech, a Haryana-based provider of solar water pumping solutions, is planning to raise funds through an IPO comprising a fresh issue of 2.55 crore equity shares and an OFS of shares worth up to Rs 235 crore by existing shareholders.

The company provides engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) services for solar power projects, with a focus on solar water pumping, rooftop solar and ground-mounted solar systems. It has proposed to utilise Rs 215 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue for working capital requirements, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

M K Sons Fine Jewels moves step closer to IPO launch after SEBI nod
M K Sons Fine Jewels, a fine jewellery retailer with five showrooms across Mumbai and Ahmedabad, has moved a step closer to launching its IPO after receiving approval from SEBI. The company had filed its IPO proposal with the capital markets regulator in May this year.

The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of 1.36 crore equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) of 34 lakh shares by promoter Ramchand Murlidhar Raimalani.

The company plans to utilise the net proceeds from the fresh issue to set up a new showroom in Maharashtra, expand an existing showroom in Gujarat, repay certain borrowings and meet general corporate requirements.

Pushp Brands IPO plans include entirely OFS
Madhya Pradesh-based packaged spices and food company Pushp Brands (India) is planning to raise funds entirely through an offer for sale (OFS), with no fresh issue component.

Its promoters, Mahendra Kumar Surana and Surendra Kumar Surana, along with investors A91 Emerging Fund I LLP and Sixth Sense Ventures, will sell 74.45 lakh shares through the OFS. This means the company will not receive any IPO money.

Paramotor Digital Technology moves closer to filing updated DRHP for IPO after SEBI nod
Paramotor Digital Technology, which provides consumer spend management, rewards and loyalty solutions, digital gifting and enterprise technology services, is the only company among the seven companies that filed IPO papers through the confidential route in May 2026. As a result, details of its proposed IPO are not publicly available.

Founded in 2016, the company offers a portfolio of products, including SpendPro, a prepaid card-based spend management platform; RewardOn, an enterprise rewards and loyalty management solution; yayyy.shop, a direct-to-consumer digital gifting marketplace; and DevStack, its enterprise technology and software development services vertical.

2.headline: Business in the Week Ahead (August 31 – September 4, 2026)
2.heading: Business in the Week Ahead (August 31 – September 4, 2026)
2.intro: Three IPOs open this week, alongside key India, US, UK and Eurozone economic data, including GDP, PMI, inflation, jobs and forex reserves releases
2.body:
The Indian equity market opened on a positive note on Friday, extending the rebound after two consecutive sessions of losses. Buying was visible across sectors, with IT stocks leading the gains, while broader market sentiment was supported by positive global cues.

At the latest update on Moneycontrol, the Sensex stood at 77,287.27, up 353.68 points. The early momentum also reflected a return of risk appetite among investors after recent weakness.

Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, said the near-term market outlook remains positive though investors are likely to remain cautious until there is greater clarity on the US Federal Reserve’s stance on interest rates. “The near-term bias is cautiously positive, supported by the stronger Gift Nifty and gains in US equities, while Asian markets remain mixed. Easing crude prices provide some relief, but investors may remain watchful ahead of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech and its implications for rate expectations,” Tailor said.

The morning trade was also helped by strength in technology stocks and a softer volatility reading, while auto, metal and realty stocks traded higher. Investors appeared to be taking advantage of lower levels, although the gains remained sensitive to global market signals and ongoing foreign fund flows.

In IPO news, three IPOs are set to hit the Indian primary market in the coming days. Pernia’s Pop-Up Studio (Purple Style Labs) will open for subscription on August 31, 2026, and close on September 2, with a price band of Rs 546– Rs 575 per share.

Deepa Jewellers and Rays of Belief will both open their IPOs on September 1, 2026, and close on September 3, 2026. Deepa Jewellers has set its price band at Rs 168– Rs 177 per share, while Rays of Belief has fixed its price band at Rs 227– Rs 239 per share.

Here are some important indicators that market participants should keep an eye out for.

Monday (August 31)

IPO: Pernia's Pop-up Studio opens

India GDP Annual Growth Rate: The Indian real gross domestic product expanded by 7.8% from the previous year in the March quarter of 2026, slowing slightly from the upwardly revised 8% growth from the earlier period. The Q2 number is to be released.

Tuesday (September 1)  

IPO: Rays of Belief IPO, Deepa Jewellers IPO opens

India Manufacturing PMI: India's HSBC Manufacturing PMI eased to 52.9 in August from 53.5 in July, marking the weakest improvement in factory conditions since August 2021. The final reading for August will be declared.

Euro Area Manufacturing PMI: The S&amp;P Global Eurozone Manufacturing PMI rose to 52.8 in August from 51.9 in the previous month, surpassing market expectations of 51.8. The final data for August will be announced.

UK Manufacturing PMI: The UK Manufacturing PMI eased to 51.5 in August, the lowest level in five months, from 51.9 in July, flash data showed. Figures for August will be released.

Euro Area Inflation Rate: Eurozone annual inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July, in line with flash estimates, up from 2.8% in June. The flash data for August will be shown.

Euro Area Consumer Price Index (CPI): Consumer Price Index CPI in the Euro Area increased to 103.24 points in July from 103.02 points in June. The flash data for August will be revealed.

US Manufacturing PMI: The S&amp;P Global US Manufacturing PMI eased to 53.2 in August from 53.9 previously, flash estimates showed. August final data will be announced.

Wednesday (September 2)

Thursday (September 3)

India Services PMI: The HSBC India Services PMI increased to 54.5 in August from 53.3 in the previous month, and above market forecasts of 53.8, according to preliminary estimates. The final reading is awaited.

Euro Area Services PMI: The S&amp;P Global Eurozone Services PMI was unchanged at 51.7 in August, slightly above market expectations of 51.5, according to flash estimates. Final reading for August will be revealed.

UK Services PMI: The S&amp;P Global UK Services PMI rose to 52.8 in August 2026 from 52.1 in July, contrasting with market forecasts of 51.8, flash estimates showed. August final numbers will be announced.

US Services PMI: The S&amp;P Global US Services PMI rose to 56.8 in August from 54.6 in the previous month, well above market expectations of a drop to 54. The final data for August is awaited.

US Initial Jobless Claims: The number of people claiming unemployment benefits in the US fell by 4,000 to 203,000 on the third week of August from 207,000 the previous week, below market expectations. Data for August 29 will be shared. 

Friday (September 4)

India Foreign Exchange Reserves: Foreign Exchange Reserves in India increased to $716.91 billion in August 14 from $707.00 billion in the previous week. The numbers for week ending August 21 will be released.
